questions.q: Why can't the Script Debugger from Lesson 26 ever be used to debug a Client Script?
options: Client Scripts are written in a completely different programming language than Business Rules
The Script Debugger only supports debugging CSS, never JavaScript
Client Scripts never contain any variables worth inspecting
Client Scripts run as real JavaScript in the user's browser, not on the server-side engine the Script Debugger attaches to
questions.explain: The Script Debugger is scoped to server-side execution. Client Scripts execute client-side, in the browser — a different runtime entirely.

options: Breakpoints cannot be set on Client Scripts under any circumstances
In the browser's DevTools Sources (or Debugger) tab, by clicking that line number on the loaded client script file
In the ServiceNow Script Debugger, the same way as a Business Rule
By adding a gs.info() call, since that's the only way to pause execution
questions.explain: Since this script runs in the browser, DevTools' Sources/Debugger tab is where a real breakpoint on it gets set — not the server-side Script Debugger.

questions.q: What does typing `g_form` directly into the DevTools Console (with a ServiceNow form open) actually do?
options: Submits the form immediately
Opens the Script Debugger automatically
Returns the live GlideForm object for the form that's currently open, so you can call its methods on demand
Throws an error, since g_form only exists inside a saved script file
questions.explain: DevTools' Console evaluates JavaScript live against the page — g_form is a real object on that page, so typing it returns its current state.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of `console.log()` over setting a breakpoint, when inspecting a Client Script?
options: It is the only way to inspect any variable in a Client Script
It automatically fixes any bug it finds
It confirms a value quickly without pausing execution at all
It permanently disables the script it's placed in
questions.explain: console.log() just prints to the Console as the script runs — useful when you want a quick trace without stopping execution to inspect state.

questions.q: Why is debugging a Client Script with DevTools considered standard practice rather than a ServiceNow-specific skill?
options: ServiceNow built a custom version of DevTools exclusively for its platform
DevTools only works on pages that are part of a ServiceNow instance
It's the exact same browser-native tooling (breakpoints, console, live evaluation) any front-end developer uses on any website, just applied to a Client Script file
Client Scripts require a special DevTools plugin not used anywhere else
questions.explain: Client Scripts are real JavaScript in a real browser, so the same DevTools workflow used on any site applies directly, with no ServiceNow-specific tooling involved.
